sources.entry: FreeCAD - FreeCAD is an open-source 3D parametric modeler

summary.one_liner: FreeCAD is an open-source parametric 3D modeler for designing real-world objects of any size, running on Windows, macOS and Linux.
summary.what_it_does: FreeCAD lets you model objects by changing parameters in a model history, so a design can be edited after it is built. You can sketch geometry-constrained 2D shapes and use them as the base for 3D objects. It provides tools to adjust dimensions and produce production drawings from 3D models. The README says it targets product design, mechanical engineering and architecture, for hobbyists, students, teachers and experienced CAD users. It is built on the OpenCASCADE geometry kernel, the Coin3D scene library, Qt for the GUI, and offers a broad Python API.
use_cases: sketching constrained 2D shapes and extruding them to 3D
learning CAD as a hobbyist or student
how_to_run: Download precompiled packages for Windows, macOS or Linux from the latest releases page
On many Linux distributions, install from the software center application
For weekly development builds, use the releases page
To build from source, follow the Developers Handbook 'Getting Started' build instructions
notable: Parametric modeling driven by an editable model history
Python API for scripting and macros
Runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
caveats: README does not state a specific limitation; building from source requires following the separate Developers Handbook
